title: Large language models reorganize representational geometry during in-context learning
abstract: arXiv:2605.28854v3 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) show remarkable flexibility in adapting to novel tasks without parameter updates, a capacity known as in-context learning (ICL). Prior work has sought to understand ICL by studying the circuits, algorithms, and representations that support it. Yet why some ICL tasks are easy to solve while others are difficult remains unresolved. In this paper, we ask whether LLMs can adapt their representations arbitrarily to solve a simple linear classification task. Specifically, we construct a family of binary classification tasks in which labels are defined by projecting LLMs' own representations onto different axes. Surprisingly, although all tasks are linearly separable by construction, their in-context learnability varies systematically across axes. We find that successful ICL is accompanied by a geometric reorganization of internal representations that increases task-relevant separability. Causal interventions th

translated_title: 大型语言模型在上下文学习中重组表征几何结构
translated_abstract: arXiv:2605.28854v3 公告类型：替换 摘要：大型语言模型（LLMs）在无需参数更新的情况下适应新任务方面表现出显著的灵活性，这种能力被称为上下文学习（ICL）。先前的研究试图通过研究支持ICL的电路、算法和表征来理解这一机制。然而，为何某些ICL任务易于解决而其他任务则困难，这一问题仍未得到解答。在本文中，我们探讨LLMs是否能任意调整其表征以解决一个简单的线性分类任务。具体来说，我们构建了一组二元分类任务，其中标签通过将LLMs自身的表征投影到不同轴上来定义。令人惊讶的是，尽管所有任务在构造上都是线性可分的，但其上下文学习的可学性在不同轴之间系统性变化。我们发现，成功的ICL伴随着内部表征的几何重组，这种重组增加了任务相关的可分性。因果干预进一步证实了这种重组的重要性。
tldr: 本文发现，大型语言模型在上下文学习中通过几何重组内部表征来提高任务可分性，这解释了不同线性分类任务的可学性差异，并通过因果干预验证了该机制的关键作用。
en_tdlr: This paper reveals that large language models reorganize internal representational geometry during in-context learning to enhance task-relevant separability, explaining variability in learnability across linear classification tasks and confirming this mechanism via causal interventions.
